name: libcxx

patches.reason: Confirmed for real (2026-08-22): the shared cxx_shared library link failed with 'undefined reference to `__dso_handle`' (referenced by memory_resource.cpp's own __cxx_global_var_init()). Same root cause and same fix shape as ../libcxxabi/recipe.json's own matching patch: this project's own crt1.o never defines __dso_handle (Bionic's real crtbegin/crtend split is not imported), extra_files above already writes src/__crt_dso_handle.cpp (a tiny CRT-owned shim providing it) into the fetched checkout, but this new source's own set(LIBCXX_SOURCES ...) list never references it at all, so the shim was written to disk but never actually compiled or linked without this patch.

patches.find:
// Both MinGW and native MSVC provide a "MSVC"-like environment
#    define _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE
patches.reason: Confirmed for real (2026-08-22) on Windows: compiling filesystem_error.cpp/chrono.cpp/... failed with `error: no type named '_locale_t' in the global namespace` (and a cascade of related errors) in __locale_dir/support/windows.h. Confirmed by reading __locale_dir/locale_base_api.h directly: that file selects windows.h's own MSVC-CRT-shaped locale backend (_locale_t/_create_locale/_free_locale/_wcreate_locale) whenever _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE is defined, which include/__config defines unconditionally for every _WIN32 target ('Both MinGW and native MSVC provide a MSVC-like environment' -- an assumption that does not hold for this project's own independent Bionic-style libc). Confirmed this project's own include/locale.h already provides the *other* (POSIX/glibc-shaped) locale_t/newlocale/freelocale/uselocale API that locale_base_api.h's own final #else branch expects -- the exact same shape Android/Bionic's own real locale.h uses, which is also why __locale_dir/locale_base_api.h has its own separate, already-correct __ANDROID__ branch for that identical situation. Scope-checked before patching: __config's own _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE-gated _WIN32 block also defines _LIBCPP_WIN32API/_LIBCPP_SHORT_WCHAR/_LIBCPP_HAS_OPEN_WITH_WCHAR/_LIBCPP_HAS_BITSCAN64, all left untouched here (real, still-correct facts about targeting Windows PE regardless of which CRT/libc backs locale support) -- only the _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE #define itself is now conditioned on !defined(__BIONIC__), narrowly matching this project's own established convention (already used project-wide, e.g. crt-libcxx-build.py's own -D__BIONIC__ compiler flag) of using __BIONIC__ as the "this is CRT's own libc, not the platform-default one" signal.

patches.reason: Identical fix and identical reasoning to the include/__config patch just above, applied to its __cxx03/ (C++03 compatibility headers) twin -- confirmed the exact same 'Both MinGW and native MSVC...' block, byte-for-byte, is duplicated there too. Patched for consistency even though it is not yet confirmed anything in this build actually includes the __cxx03 tree (kept in sync so a future -std=c++03 consumer does not silently hit the same MSVC-locale-backend error this patch just fixed for the default headers).

Confirmed for real (2026-08-22) on Windows: `fatal error: 'io.h' file not found` compiling print.cpp (its own #include <io.h> under _LIBCPP_WIN32API, for _get_osfhandle() -- confirmed by reading the fetched file directly). <io.h> is an MSVC/mingw-CRT-specific header this project's own independent libc has no equivalent of (it has its own internal fd->HANDLE mapping, private to libc/src/arch/windows/common/syscall.c's own static get_fd_handle(), not part of any public/stable API surface worth exposing just for this). Rather than inventing a new public libc entry point purely to feed a `_get_osfhandle`-shaped shim, redirect print's own terminal-detection to the already-fully-working, already-portable isatty()-based path every other platform uses -- confirmed this project's own libc/src/fd.c already implements isatty() cross-platform (including a real, working Windows implementation backed by GetFileType(), used today by termios.c/process.c/syslog.c). The cost is std::print's own native-Unicode WriteConsoleW() fast path on a real Windows console (__write_to_windows_console(), also gated by the same macro) -- accepted as a real, honest, narrow degradation (falls back to plain byte-oriented fwrite(), matching every other stream write this project already does) rather than either reimplementing MSVC's fd model or leaving the whole recipe unbuildable on Windows. A single #undef right after _LIBCPP_BEGIN_NAMESPACE_STD (rather than 6 separate find/replace patches at every individual _LIBCPP_WIN32API check in this file) is deliberately used to flip all of this file's own downstream dispatch consistently in one place, scope-checked to confirm nothing this header transitively includes reads the same macro.

Companion patch to ../include/print's own matching entry -- must be applied together, since include/print declares __is_windows_terminal()/__is_posix_terminal() based on this exact macro and src/print.cpp is what actually *defines* one or the other; patching only one side leaves either an undefined symbol at link time (header expects __is_windows_terminal but this file never defines it) or an unused/never-called definition. Confirmed for real (2026-08-22): this file's own #if defined(_LIBCPP_WIN32API) block is the only place in it that reads the macro (grepped directly), so this single #undef consistently redirects all of this file's own logic to the __is_posix_terminal branch, matching include/print's own patched dispatch.

notes: libc/src/errno added (2026-08-22, same session): libc/src/__support/str_to_integer.h's own #include "src/errno/libc_errno.h" needs it, confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'src/errno/libc_errno.h' file not found`. Tiny (3 files: CMakeLists.txt, libc_errno.cpp, libc_errno.h, confirmed via `git ls-tree`) and self-contained -- its own includes (src/__support/macros/*, hdr/errno_macros.h) were already satisfied by the directories fetched earlier. Deliberately NOT the fetch-the-whole-parent-directory shortcut used for libc/include just above: libc/src/ as a whole is 2814 files, the real OS-specific llvm-libc *implementation* (math/, string/, stdio/, ...) this project has no use for at all (it has its own complete libc) -- only this one narrow subdirectory was actually needed, so only this one was added.

libc/include added (the whole directory, 304 files, confirmed via `git ls-tree -r`) after libc/src/__support/macros/properties/types.h's own unconditional #include "include/llvm-libc-macros/float16-macros.h" -- confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'include/llvm-libc-macros/float16-macros.h' file not found`. Unlike libc/hdr/'s own files, this one is not LIBC_FULL_BUILD-gated overlay-mode code -- it is real, always-needed content (plain macro/type definitions, confirmed as plain committed files, not .h.def templates needing generation). Fetched the whole directory rather than just llvm-libc-macros/ (which alone would have been enough for this one error) to front-load the very likely next miss, llvm-libc-types/ (a standard sibling in llvm-libc's own include/ layout) -- avoiding another full rebuild-and-discover round trip for a directory of comparable, still-bounded size (304 files total is not remotely close to needing the rest of llvm-libc's own OS-specific implementation).

libc/hdr added alongside libc/shared and libc/src/__support (2026-08-22, same session): libc/src/__support/CPP/limits.h's own #include "hdr/limits_macros.h" needs it, confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'hdr/limits_macros.h' file not found`. Small (66 files, confirmed via `git ls-tree -r`) and, unlike __support/, genuinely reassuring to depend on rather than just bounded: limits_macros.h's own content is a plain `#ifdef LIBC_FULL_BUILD ... #else #include <limits.h> #endif` -- llvm-libc's own "overlay mode" escape hatch, deliberately meant for exactly this project's own situation (reusing llvm-libc's portable support utilities layered on top of a real, independent host libc, never building the rest of llvm-libc itself). LIBC_FULL_BUILD is never defined anywhere in this project's own build, so every libc/hdr/*.h wrapper takes the "Overlay mode" branch -- confirmed on errno_macros.h too (same #ifdef LIBC_FULL_BUILD/#else/#include <errno.h>/#endif shape), and on one libc/hdr/func/*.h proxy (aligned_alloc.h), which instead of a direct #include <...> redirects to a sibling libc/hdr/*_overlay.h file within this same small directory -- still fully self-contained within the 66 files fetched here, not a further external dependency.

libc/src/__support added alongside libc/shared (2026-08-22, same session as the libc/shared fix just below): libc/shared/fp_bits.h's own #include "src/__support/FPUtil/FPBits.h" reaches further into llvm-libc's own internal support-utility tree, confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'src/__support/FPUtil/FPBits.h' file not found` the first time libc/shared alone was fetched. libc/src/__support/ (319 files total, confirmed via `git ls-tree -r`) is llvm-libc's own deliberately reusable, OS-independent low-level utility layer -- CPP/ (portable STL-shaped helpers: bit.h, type_traits.h, array.h, ...), macros/, math_extras.h, sign.h, uint128.h, etc. -- not the OS-specific syscall implementation the rest of llvm-libc's own src/ tree has, so fetching the whole subtree here (rather than chasing individual transitive headers one at a time) is a bounded, deliberate scope match to what FPBits.h actually needs, not a slippery-slope pull of all of llvm-libc. No new include path was needed for this addition: it resolves through the exact same CRT_LIBC_SHARED_PARENT_DIR (-I<...>/libc) the driver already adds for libc/shared, since "src/__support/..." is *also* rooted at that same libc/ parent directory.

build_targets no longer includes cxx_filesystem or cxx-generated-config (both present in the OLD recipe's own list, the second one Windows-only). Confirmed for real: `ninja -t targets` against this new source's own configured build tree lists only cxx, cxx_experimental, cxx_shared, cxx_static, cxx-test-depends -- neither name exists as a target at all any more, on any platform (surfaced as `ninja: error: unknown target 'cxx_filesystem'`, not a per-platform gate the way the OLD recipe's own Windows-only omission was). Matches a real, general modernization in current libcxx: C++17 <filesystem> is no longer a separate opt-in library needing its own build target.

generate-cxx-headers added to build_targets (2026-08-22, same session): correcting an overclaim in the note above -- header generation is NOT fully folded into cxx's own build graph. `cmake --install` failed after a full `cxx`+`cxx_experimental` build with `file INSTALL cannot find .../include/c++/v1/libcxx.imp: No such file or directory`. Confirmed via the real libcxx/include/CMakeLists.txt (fetched and read at this pinned commit): libcxx.imp is one output of add_custom_target(generate-cxx-headers ALL DEPENDS ${_all_includes}) -- an IWYU mapping file generated by utils/generate_iwyu_mapping.py, listed in install(FILES ... COMPONENT cxx-headers) alongside the real headers. The plain per-header copies DO get pulled in transitively by cxx/cxx_experimental (since compiling needs them), but this one extra generated file apparently isn't a hard dependency of the compiled objects themselves, so ninja never built it when only cxx/cxx_experimental were requested -- confirmed via the WSL build tree directly: the file was genuinely absent from the build dir (`ls .../include/c++/v1/ | grep imp` -> nothing) and no "Generate the mapping file for include-what-you-use" line ever appeared in the build log. `ninja -t targets all` confirms a plain `generate-cxx-headers: phony` alias exists (in addition to the subdir-prefixed `libcxx/include/generate-cxx-headers`), so requesting it directly as its own build target is the fix, not a deeper CMakeLists.txt change.

2026-08-22: MIGRATED off the old source.repository (platform/external/libcxx) -- confirmed dead: its own refs/heads/main tip is the exact commit this recipe had pinned since 2026-08-21, and that commit's own message is "Empty merge ab/12770256 into aosp-main-future" (2024-12-20), a placeholder with no real content change. Root cause of the C++20 <bit> gap that motivated this migration: that frozen fork's own include/bit has only 158 lines total -- the pre-existing internal __popcount() helpers, no _LIBCPP_STD_VER gating and no public std::countl_zero/countr_zero/popcount entry points at all -- confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed. Moved to toolchain/llvm-project's own libcxx/ subtree instead (the same repo ../libunwind/recipe.json already correctly uses, for the same underlying reason -- see that file's own note: "Android removed the old platform/external/libunwind project in 2021"; libcxx suffered the identical fate, just without a recipe.json update to match at the time). Confirmed for real before migrating, not assumed: fetched toolchain/llvm-project's own libcxx/include/bit at this exact pinned commit and found real _LIBCPP_STD_VER >= 20/>= 23 gating and a real `constexpr int countl_zero(T x) noexcept; // C++20` declaration.

source.ref reuses ../libunwind/recipe.json's own already-pinned commit (37f38d1f3276b62fba09462ab4807dce846c732d) rather than picking a separate, newer one -- all three recipes now describe one single, consistent, real point-in-time snapshot of the same monorepo instead of three independently-drifting pins into the same repo.

cmake.driver (new): the fetched libcxx/CMakeLists.txt at this commit no longer calls project() itself at all (confirmed by grepping the full ~860-line file for `^project(` -- zero matches) -- unlike the OLD platform/external/libcxx fork, which still carried its own standalone-build bootstrap (the exact asymmetry ../libunwind/standalone/CMakeLists.txt's own comment already described between libunwind and "the sibling libcxx/libcxxabi checkouts" was true when that comment was written, but libcxx has since converged onto the same monorepo-only, add_subdirectory()-only structure libunwind already had). Needs the identical driver-CMakeLists.txt treatment libunwind already established: libstdc++/third_party/libcxx/standalone/CMakeLists.txt calls project() for real and add_subdirectory()s CRT_LIBCXX_SOURCE_DIR (the actual fetched checkout, passed by tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's own cmake.driver handling).

extra_checkout_dirs (cmake/, runtimes/cmake/): same reason as ../libunwind/recipe.json's own matching note -- libcxx/CMakeLists.txt's own CMAKE_MODULE_PATH references "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../cmake" and "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../runtimes/cmake/Modules" directly, confirmed by reading the fetched file. Shared with libunwind/libcxxabi's own fetch of the identical two directories (tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's fetch_recipe() already copies extra_checkout_dirs idempotently, skipping a directory that another recipe already staged).

LIBCXX_STANDARD_VER (removed): the previous pin (c++14) was chosen for a reason specific to the OLD, now-abandoned fork ("avoids the removed C11 gets() import") that does not obviously still apply to this genuinely different, actively-maintained source tree, and this CMake option controls the dialect libcxx's *own* .cpp implementation files are compiled with -- a materially different axis from _LIBCPP_STD_VER (which real *consumers* like Skia's own -std=c++20 TUs see, driven by their own compiler flag, not by how libcxx.a/.so itself was built). Left unset for now (upstream's own default) rather than carried forward on stale reasoning; revisit with a real, evidenced reason if the build actually needs an explicit value.

LIBCXX_CXX_ABI=system-libcxxabi (changed from the OLD recipe's own plain 'libcxxabi' value) -- a real, forced architectural finding, not a style choice. The new source's own libcxx/cmake/Modules/HandleLibCXXABI.cmake, included via libcxx/CMakeLists.txt's `include(HandleLibCXXABI)`, only wires up the plain 'libcxxabi' branch's libcxx-abi-shared/libcxx-abi-static targets `if (TARGET cxxabi_shared)`/`if (TARGET cxxabi_static)` -- i.e. it requires libcxxabi's own CMake targets to already exist in the *same* CMake project graph, which only a combined, single-configure "runtimes" build (libcxx+libcxxabi add_subdirectory()'d together under one project()) provides. This project's own architecture deliberately builds each recipe as a fully separate `cmake -S -B` invocation instead (see ../libunwind/recipe.json's own notes for why: no combined-runtimes-build machinery, by design), so that branch silently produced no libcxx-abi-shared/-static targets at all -- confirmed for real via `CMake Error ... Target "libcxx-abi-shared" not found` at libcxx/src/CMakeLists.txt's own add_custom_command generator-expression evaluation, plus a CMake Warning that LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS/LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_LIBRARY_PATH (this recipe's own, still set) were going completely unused. The 'system-libcxxabi' branch is the one still designed for exactly this project's own case: a real, separately-built libc++abi provided out of tree, located by name+path rather than an in-process CMake target -- import_shared_library(libcxx-abi-shared c++abi)/import_static_library(..., c++abi) match this recipe's own libcxxabi output naming exactly (libc++abi.a/.so/.dll), and import_private_headers() copies exactly cxxabi.h/__cxxabi_config.h from LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS -- both confirmed present in ../libcxxabi's own fetched include/ directory before making this change. LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS/LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_LIBRARY_PATH themselves needed no change at all, only the LIBCXX_CXX_ABI value selecting which branch of HandleLibCXXABI.cmake consumes them.

patches: started empty, not migrated blind. Every one of the OLD recipe's patches (six-plus _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE-family __locale/__config/locale.cpp/system_error.cpp/config_elast.h redirects, the lib/CMakeLists.txt win32-sources exclusion, the two shared-library visibility/RUNTIME-DESTINATION fixes) was written against the OLD fork's exact file layout and line content, none assumed to still apply to this genuinely different, actively-maintained source -- LLVM's own libcxx has been substantially reorganized (header modularization, __config split, etc.) since that fork was frozen. One has since been rediscovered for real (Linux was reached first this migration): the __dso_handle wiring, now recorded in the patches array above, needed again but in a simpler shape (a direct list insertion) than the OLD patch's own "insert before a conditional block" approach. The rest (all Windows-specific, or MSVC-STL-related) have not been re-encountered yet.
